subject: G-501-091 — Table 5/6 meds at the phone check
body:
Hi Maya,

G-501-091 had the W2 call yesterday, 20 Aug (baseline 06 Aug). Med list reconciled with participant and spouse; source and EDC match.

He remains on buspirone and rosuvastatin. Dr Chen reviewed both against the appendix and documented a wide therapeutic index for this participant. No med-monitor consult was requested. We asked specifically about anxiety control for the buspirone, and reviewed the rosuvastatin prescribing-information adverse effects with him. No loss of anxiety control, muscle symptoms, or other new complaints. Neither prescriber wants a dose change.

Compliance check, unused-pack reminder and contraception review also done. He's worried that seeing the drugs in the tables means he should stop them, so we reinforced not changing his regular meds without his treating clinician.

Can you confirm the monitor worksheet can say 'permitted with monitoring' rather than 'washout pending'? The worksheet currently auto-populates 7 days for both names.

Thanks,
Lena

subject: ATE packet G-582-014 — missing forms explained
body:
Mara,

Closing out the 9 Sep ATE Week 28 packet for G-582-014. Everything collected was entered on 10 Sep.

The biomarker blood draw was attempted by two staff members, three sticks total, without obtaining a sample. Attempts and outcome are in source and the collection page says attempted/no sample. We did not open a PD entry for this.

ALSAQ-40 wasn't administered because of the participant's language barrier. That reason is in source and EDC, rather than a score or a PD number. The other PROs were completed using the available approved language versions. His wife wrote the ROADS answers because of his hand weakness; he selected every answer, and she didn't suggest any.

The rest of the visit packet is complete. Just flagging the blank pages so you don't have to chase them during review.

Jules

subject: G-504-043 remote W8 source is filed
body:
Hi team,

Recap for G-504-043, baseline 03-Aug, W8 completed by video 28-Sep. His progressive disability now makes the trip unsafe; PI documented the reason for remote services.

We completed the selected remote assessments, including ALSFRS-R, CNS-BFS, C-SSRS, AE/med review and contraception review. Remote nurse did the safety labs and postdose PK. Central-lab pickup was unavailable at his address, so safety labs went to his local hospital lab. Study drug shipment and compliance records are filed.

Two notes for the monitor: weight could not be obtained because he could not safely transfer, and the optional DNA tube was finally collected with this draw—baseline DNA was unusable. We documented the weight limitation in source/EDC but did not put it on the deviation log. Other procedures not available remotely are documented per the remote-visit worksheet.

Thanks,
Priya

subject: G-503-014 — Sunday dose question / tube teaching
body:
Hi Rachel,

Closing the loop on yesterday's caregiver call. G-503-014 forgot the usual morning dose on 06 Sep and remembered at 20:15 that evening. Both packets were given together through the J-tube, reconstituted in water, finished at 20:24. No other study dose that day. This morning, 07 Sep, they went back to the usual 08:00 dose.

Caregiver asked whether they should leave a full 24 hours between those doses. I told her not to skip this morning solely because Sunday's dose was late, and reviewed the same-day versus next-day missed-dose instructions. The late dose and teaching are in source. No symptoms reported.

Also, the thickener question from last week was for days he takes it orally, not for putting thickener down the tube. We confirmed that oral administration with thickener is an option if needed.

Can you confirm the tube route doesn't itself require stopping IP? He's otherwise continuing the study.

Thanks,
Maya

subject: G-509-189 unscheduled assessment completed
body:
Dr. K / Maria,

Closing the loop on G-509-189's 06 Oct unscheduled clinic assessment. She called with mild nausea and a late period. Dr. K arranged a same-day visit; no study-dose change or interruption was made and she did not require admission.

We ran a urine pregnancy test in clinic (negative). Because of the symptoms and delayed period, Dr. K also ordered a local serum hCG that afternoon; negative result received before close of business. Her usual IUS plus husband's latex condoms were verbally reconfirmed, with no reported lapse, and documented in source and the visit CRF.

Nausea began 05 Oct. Dr. K assessed it as mild, non-serious and unrelated. We entered the AE in source and EDC on 06 Oct, including onset, severity, seriousness, relationship, action taken and outcome. At the 07 Oct check-in she reported nausea resolved; resolution and outcome were updated in EDC that day. No pregnancy Key Study Event was opened because both tests were negative.

ECG was completed with the other in-clinic safety assessments. No unscheduled PK was obtained: mild event, no dose modification/interruption and no severe event requiring evaluation.

Signed lab reports are now uploaded.

Leah

subject: Reconsent packet returned, G-503-123
body:
Maria,

Originals arrived yesterday, 26 Aug, for G-503-123. These were the Master and G updates requiring reconsent. Both were ready for use on 17 Aug, and his next visit was the scheduled 20 Aug clinic visit converted to telemedicine because travel was unsafe with his disability.

We sent both approved forms on 18 Aug. He read them but left them unsigned. Dr Chen, who is trained and delegated for consent, reviewed Master first and then G on video on 20 Aug, answered questions, and watched him sign/date each after its discussion. He accepted the opportunity to speak with a physician Investigator—Dr Chen did that discussion and documented it.

Dr Chen did NOT sign the scans that day. We used the prepaid return envelope; on receipt of the originals on 26 Aug she signed/dated both with the actual receipt-day date. Fully executed copies went back to the participant that afternoon, with the originals retained here. The worksheet explains why the participant and investigator dates differ.

Please leave the envelope receipt with the consent source when you finish review. Thx.

subject: Administrative G screen failure — no G visit billed
body:
Hi team,

G-523-021 passed Master screening on 02 Sep and was assigned to G through IRT on 03 Sep. During scheduling that afternoon she mentioned a seizure on 09 Aug; the hospital note confirms it. We knew this before booking the G visit.

We entered an administrative G screen failure with the seizure reason, without obtaining a G consent or doing G screening procedures. She was immediately reassigned through IRT to another available regimen on 04 Sep. That regimen's team independently reviewed its criteria and handled its own consent; we have not represented her as eligible there just because she passed Master.

Master demographics/NeuroSTAMP and assessed eligibility are in EDC, as is the G ineligibility reason. Finance asked whether a G screening visit occurred: no, only the admin action.

Please confirm the visit grid matches that history.

Leah

subject: G-521-014 — eligibility packet ready for review
body:
Hi Maya,

I've uploaded the final screening packet for G-521-014. Master consent and screening were 08 Sep; we held assignment while Dr. Lin reviewed the labs and breathing results.

Initial SVC on 08 Sep was 48% predicted. We brought him back on 11 Sep, still in the initial screening period: three mask trials with our certified evaluator were 47%, 49%, and 50%. The worksheet carries 50%, not the mean.

ALT on 08 Sep was 126 U/L, local ULN 40. Repeat on 11 Sep was 120, AST normal, eGFR 64. Dr. Lin reviewed the repeat and documented that the residual ALT elevation was not clinically significant; no unstable liver condition. All other eligibility items passed. Assignment was released 14 Sep and combined G screening/baseline was 21 Sep.

Can you check that both lab reports are visible? The first report was initially filed under outside records.

Thanks,
Jess

subject: RE: G-514-103 remote W8 and local draw
body:
Hi all,

Closing the loop on yesterday's visit (28 Sep 2026). Baseline was 03 Aug 2026.

Dr Shah documented that the participant's progressive mobility limitation makes transport unsafe. Video worked, so we used telemedicine with remote services for W8. ALSFRS-R, Since Last Visit C-SSRS, AE and med review, compliance review and CNS-BFS were completed by trained/delegated staff. No positive suicide responses. The procedures we couldn't do remotely are identified in source and EDC with the disability reason, not left as unexplained blanks.

Central lab transport wasn't feasible at her address this week. The home service used the local laboratory for the requested safety panel; report is filed and Dr Shah reviewed it. Drug shipment is documented per the MOP.

She mentioned mild seasonal nasal congestion, now resolved. Dr Shah assessed it as mild, nonserious and unrelated; onset, resolution, action and outcome are in the AE form and EDC. No drug interruption or dose change.

Please keep the transport request open for the next clinic visit rather than canceling it permanently.

Rita

subject: G-534-119 phone note / packet counts
body:
Megan,

Quick answer to your query: the Aug 24 contact was the ATE W2 telephone visit for G-534-119, following the Aug 10 W24 clinic visit.

I asked how he was taking the drug and specifically about missed doses; he reports two packs daily and none missed. I did not ask his wife to lay out and count every packet on the phone. We reviewed meds, AEs and their current contraception, and reminded them to bring the drug and unused containers to W4. No new AEs.

There is no ALSFRS-R for that call. The phone worksheet is signed and filed. Please let me know if the compliance narrative is not displaying in your view.

—Sam

subject: G-501-101 consent/source timing for your review
body:
Hi Maria,

Putting the sequence here before you review the screening chart. On 03 Aug the clinic MA did weight and vitals at 08:10 for the patient's regular ALS clinic appointment. Those were routine care, not ordered for research. We used those values in the screening source later.

At 09:00 Anne, our study-trained RN delegated for consent, started the Master discussion. She covered the purpose, endpoints, procedures, risks/possible benefits and the right to decline or stop without affecting care. Patient had read the approved ICF at home and asked several questions. He declined an additional discussion with a physician Investigator; that choice is in Anne's note. Signed/dated at 09:48, fully executed copy handed to him, original filed with the SI. Research assessments started at 10:05.

Master eligibility was confirmed and assignment to G returned on 04 Aug. Anne then did the G discussion and written consent in person, before G screening. Same copy/original arrangements. No baseline dosing yet.

Can you confirm that we don't need to repeat the routine-care vitals just because their timestamp precedes the Master signature?

Thanks,
Leah

subject: G-501-041 baseline LP date / DNA redraw completed
body:
Hi Maya,

Closing the loop on the two sample queries before your visit. G-501-041 had Regimen G eligibility confirmed on 09 Aug. The optional LP was done 10 Aug at 09:10, biomarkers only. First study dose was administered in clinic on 17 Aug at 09:30 after the remaining baseline procedures were finished. The LP consent was already signed before the collection.

The baseline DNA tube wasn't usable, so we obtained another on 25 Aug. Participant was happy to come back just for that; no repeat LP or other baseline assessments were done. Both collection dates are entered under their actual dates, not backdated to baseline.

Can you close the DNA query when you review? I've put the replacement accession next to the original accession in the sample tracker.

Thanks,
Jess

subject: G-512-061 W8 respiratory worksheet — please close query?
body:
Hi Maya,

G-512-061 was here 29 Sep for W8 (BL 04 Aug). Can you take another look at the query asking why we stopped after three SVC blows?

Upright, mask, study spirometer. Values were 2.80, 2.56 and 2.41 L. We retained the entire printout and entered all three values on the CRF. The worksheet uses 2.80 L as the highest result. No extra attempts were made. Rater is current for NEALS SVC/ALSFRS-R and delegated.

Rest of W8 checklist done, including strength and CNS-BFS. He took his regular dose at home at 07:30; PK was drawn here at 10:05. Pharmacy reconciled the returned packets before dispensing.

Thanks,
Lena

subject: Monitoring follow-up: G-591-862 incomplete W8 fields
body:
Dear site team,

Thank you for the source review yesterday. This is my recap for G-591-862, baseline 03 Aug, W8 on 28 Sep.

The strength assessor attempted the scheduled testing, but progressive upper-limb disability prevented a usable result. The safety blood draw was attempted at several sites without success; the investigator reviewed the situation and arranged a successful repeat on 30 Sep. SVC and the other scheduled assessments were completed.

CNS-BFS was not administered because of the participant's language barrier. The reason is recorded in source and EDC. ALSFRS-R was completed with the delegated, currently NEALS-certified backup evaluator rather than the usual evaluator, who was absent. The assessor documented the participant's answers and the interpreter's involvement. C-SSRS was completed by the certified nurse.

The three incomplete fields initially appeared on the export as blank. Your team has now supplied the reasons and linked the repeat laboratory results. No new clinical event was identified in the AE review. Please retain those explanatory records with the visit source.

Regards,
Martin

subject: G-546-007 — ATE nausea hold resolved
body:
Hi all,

Recap for G-546-007. On 14 Sep he called before his morning ATE dose with moderate nausea interfering with meals. Dr Patel assessed him in clinic that morning and discussed with the MM before withholding IP. Last dose had been 13 Sep at 08:00. An unscheduled PK was obtained during the 14 Sep assessment, with last-dose time on the requisition.

AE entered with onset, severity, nonserious status, relatedness assessment, action taken and outcome. No hospitalization or other seriousness criteria; Dr Patel did not identify any study-wide conduct implications.

We reviewed symptoms by phone during the hold. On 28 Sep, following resolution, Dr Patel and the MM agreed to restart the randomized ATE dose of two packets/200 mg each morning. No unblinding requested or performed. He restarted that day and reported tolerating it on today's call.

Please retain this with the dose-history reconciliation. The next scheduled visit remains unchanged.

Anika

subject: G-511-018 — W24 handoff complete; removing duplicate safety-call task
body:
Hi Morgan,

Closing out yesterday's visit (18 Aug) for G-511-018. This was the scheduled W24 visit, not a withdrawal. Participant elected to continue into ATE.

All W24 assessments, including the exit questionnaire and vital status, are filed. Pharmacy held the ATE dose until the visit procedures were finished; predose/postdose PK were obtained per the worksheet. No placebo-period dose was taken that morning. ATE supply was dispensed and the next visit is booked.

Our calendar automatically created a placebo-period follow-up safety call when I closed the blinded kit record. I'm deleting that duplicate task, not the eventual post-ATE safety call. Please leave the participant active in the tracking report — the word 'exit' on the questionnaire seems to be what tripped the report.

Thanks,
Elena

body:

To: Regimen G team

Itraconazole was dispensed to G-507-097 today following yesterday's outside prescription for a fungal nail condition. Dr Williams reviewed the diagnosis, medical status and complete medication list, considered the treatment necessary, and approved coadministration. Participant started it this morning.
